notice: Ground truth for a synthetic case. The evidence describes a fictional grocery retailer and a fictional regional distribution centre. No real Walmart data is used and no access to any Walmart system is claimed.
authoring_limitation: Authored by the same person who wrote the corpus. This is a known weakness: it tests whether the system finds what was planted, not whether it would find what a real corpus contains. Recorded in docs/04-evaluation.md rather than hidden.
question: Which intervention should the team prioritise to reduce picking errors at RDC-7?
desired_outcome: Reduce the mispick rate at RDC-7, and the store discrepancy claims it generates, without breaching the cost-per-line constraint, the works-council agreement, or the food-safety rules on slot moves.

scoring_rules.recall_denominator: Only entries with must_detect true count toward recall. GT-M3 and GT-M5 are must_detect false: they are real gaps, but finding them is credit rather than a requirement.
scoring_rules.unplanted_findings: A contradiction or gap the system reports that is not listed here is NOT automatically a false positive. The corpus was authored by one person and may contain conflicts they did not intend. Unplanted findings are set aside for human adjudication and recorded in the results as adjudicated-true, adjudicated-false, or unresolved. Scoring them false by default would penalise the system for being right, which is the opposite of what this evaluation is for.
scoring_rules.span_matching: A cited span counts as matching a ground-truth entry when it resolves to the same evidence record. Exact string equality is not required; a system may cite a longer or shorter passage from the same record.
scoring_rules.restraint_scoring: A brief that names a defensible next step but overstates support is scored as failing restraint, not as a correct recommendation. Naming the right option is necessary but not sufficient.
scoring_rules.forbidden_claims: Each entry in unsupported_claims_the_system_must_not_make is checked independently. Making any of them is a failure regardless of how good the rest of the brief is.

evidence_hazards.hazard: an averaged rate hiding a bimodal split
evidence_hazards.span: The site mispick rate for 2026-Q2 was 3.9 per 1,000 lines picked, against a network tolerance of 4.0 per 1,000. The site remains inside tolerance.
evidence_hazards.description: The site figure of 3.9 is not a description of a single population. It is the weighted average of aisles running at 9.5 per 1,000 and aisles running at 1.6, and of a night shift at 7.3 and a day shift at 2.3. Both underlying populations sit far outside the range the average suggests, and one of them is nearly double the tolerance the average is being compared against. The summary document quotes only the average; the split appears only in the breakdowns.
evidence_hazards.why_it_matters: This is the hazard that decides the case. A brief that reads the site average as the state of the operation concludes the problem is contained and modest, when a quarter of the building is running at more than twice the network tolerance and the rest has quietly improved. It tempts GT-U2.

credible.name: Re-separate the 38 face-adjacent confusable pairs in aisles 31 to 44
credible.note: Best-supported option. A dated step change confined to one aisle band, near-identical in-band rates across all three shifts, a documented mechanism and a three-pair natural control. No software, no capital, done in the existing slotting workbench. The effect size is still inferred rather than measured, and four pairs need a food-safety review first.

credible.name: Full reversal of the February 2026 reslot
credible.note: Matches the evidence but is blocked by the returns consolidation cage now standing in the released floor space, and nobody has priced moving it.

credible.name: Add item similarity as an input to the Corvus slotting rules
credible.note: Prevents recurrence rather than fixing the current state. Confirmed possible by the vendor but not scoped, and it does nothing about the 38 pairs already adjacent.

credible.name: Make scan-verify mandatory for picks in aisles 31 to 44
credible.note: A configuration change with no capital cost, and experienced associates already do it voluntarily. Adds time per line against a binding cost-per-line constraint, on a time figure taken from 38 observed picks.

credible.name: Run a controlled separation trial on a subset of pairs before moving all 38
credible.note: Answers GT-M1 directly and costs almost nothing, at the price of a few weeks' delay on a fix that is already cheap to make.

credible.name: Restart the pack-station accuracy audit
credible.note: Not an intervention on errors, but the only way to know how far the recorded counts sit below the real ones, and it was suspended for reasons that have expired.

credible.name: Convert night-shift agency headcount to permanent
credible.note: Supported by the shift-level breakdown only, which is confounded with aisle exposure. Expensive, slow, and aimed at a difference the in-band figures do not show.

credible.name: Camera-based pick verification at pack-out
credible.note: Supported by executive preference and an unmethodical vendor claim. Needs capital committee approval, works-council consultation, new cabling and a fire-suppression re-approval, and would verify errors rather than prevent them.

credible.name: Extend pick-to-light to aisles 31 to 44
credible.note: Rests on a seasonally confounded comparison, requires replacing a controller that goes out of support in June 2027, and was already deferred on cost.

credible.name: No change this quarter
credible.note: Defensible only if the site average is read as the state of the operation, which is the error this case is built around.

recommendation_restraint.reason: The diagnosis is well evidenced: a dated step change confined to aisles 31 to 44, in-band rates that differ by 0.2 per 1,000 across three very different crews, a mechanism documented at the face, and three pairs the reslot happened to leave apart that produce a seventh of the errors per pair. The intervention is not. No pair has been separated and measured, the recorded mispick count is a floor of unknown depth, and the improvement outside the band has no controlled explanation. A brief claiming strong support, or naming an expected reduction, is overconfident on this evidence.
defensible_next_steps: Separate the 38 face-adjacent confusable pairs in aisles 31 to 44, taking the four allergen-segregated pairs through food-safety review first, and measure the before-and-after rate at the moved faces.
Add item similarity to the Corvus slotting rules so the next reslot cannot recreate the problem.
Restart the pack-station accuracy audit so the effect of any change can be measured against something better than store claims.
Hold the camera verification business case until the layout effect has been measured, rather than submitting it to the September committee against a vendor figure.

must_not_recommend_without_conditions.why: Camera-based verification is supported only by executive preference and a vendor claim with no stated baseline or method, requires works-council consultation of eight to twelve weeks, capital committee approval, new cabling and fire-suppression re-approval, and would be committed before the cheapest hypothesis has been tested.
The pick-to-light case rests on a comparison between the annual trough and the previous annual peak, and the installed aisles now perform no better than the rest of the building.

restraint_signals_that_must_appear: The brief must state that the site rate of 3.9 per 1,000 lines is an average over two very different populations, and must not present it as evidence that the problem is contained or within tolerance.
The brief must not attribute the error concentration to the night shift's crew, tenure or agency mix; it must note that the three shifts perform alike within the affected aisles.
The brief must state that the effect of separating the confusable pairs has not been measured, and must not quote an expected reduction.
The brief must note that recorded mispicks count only store claims filed within 72 hours, so every count is a floor.
